name: alm_stress_test
summary: Run an ALM stress test: worst-case EVE decline vs Tier-1 capital.
description:
[REGULATORY] BCBS d368. Computes ΔEVE across the six standard shocks and
expresses the worst-case loss as a fraction of Tier-1 capital (the
supervisory outlier ratio).

name: asset_liability_mismatch_index
summary: Asset-liability mismatch index from duration-weighted exposures.
description:
Index = normalised absolute duration gap
``|D_A·A − D_L·L| / A`` — zero when the book is perfectly immunised.

name: balance_sheet_projection_model
summary: Project the balance sheet and NII forward over ``n_years``.
description:
Assets and liabilities grow geometrically; equity is the residual; NII each
year is ``assets·yield − liabilities·cost``. Returns the projected paths.

name: basis_risk_irrbb
summary: Basis risk: NII impact of imperfectly-correlated index repricing.
description:
[REGULATORY] BCBS d368 — basis risk arises when assets and liabilities
reprice off different indices. ΔNII = Σ A·Δi_A − Σ L·Δi_L.

name: behavioural_modelling_nmds
summary: Model non-maturity-deposit (NMD) run-off splitting core / non-core.
description:
[REGULATORY] BCBS d368 NMD treatment. Core deposits are stable and decay
slowly; non-core (volatile) deposits run off quickly. Returns the projected
surviving balance and the effective average life.

name: convexity_gap
summary: Convexity gap of the banking book.
description:
``CGAP = C_A − (L/A)·C_L`` — the second-order term refining the
duration-gap EVE estimate ``ΔEVE ≈ A(−DGAP·Δy + ½·CGAP·Δy²)``.

name: core_deposit_duration
summary: Effective duration of core deposits modelled as a decaying annuity.
description:
Core deposits run off at ``decay_rate`` (exponential). The duration is the
PV-weighted average life of the run-off cashflows discounted at
``discount_rate`` — typically multi-year, which is why NMDs anchor the
liability side of the duration gap.

name: duration_gap_analysis
summary: Duration-gap analysis of the banking book.
description:
Duration gap ``DGAP = D_A − (L/A)·D_L``. The change in economic value of
equity for a rate shock is approximately ``ΔEVE ≈ −DGAP · A · Δy``.

name: dynamic_gap_analysis
summary: Dynamic gap projecting balance growth over future periods.
description:
Applies per-bucket growth rates compounding over ``n_periods`` and returns
the projected gap path — capturing new business unlike a static gap.

name: economic_value_of_equity_eve
summary: Economic Value of Equity: PV(assets) − PV(liabilities).
description:
[REGULATORY] BCBS d368. EVE is the residual economic value accruing to
equity holders after discounting all banking-book cashflows.

name: effective_duration_alm
summary: Effective duration of an ALM position from re-valued PVs under a shock.
description:
``D_eff = (PV− − PV+) / (2 · PV0 · Δy)`` — captures optionality in deposits,
prepayments and caps/floors that analytic duration misses.

name: eve_sensitivity_analysis
summary: EVE sensitivity (ΔEVE) under each of the six IRRBB rate shocks.
description:
[REGULATORY] BCBS d368. Reports ΔEVE for every prescribed scenario and the
worst case — the headline supervisory metric.

name: ftp_curve_construction
summary: Construct a matched-maturity FTP curve = base curve + liquidity spread.
description:
Each tenor's transfer rate adds a term-liquidity spread to the base funding
curve. The curve is non-decreasing in the spread component by construction.

name: funds_transfer_pricing_ftp
summary: Funds-transfer-price a single deal into margin components.
description:
For an asset, the lending unit earns ``customer_rate − ftp_rate`` (credit /
commercial margin) while the central treasury earns the FTP minus its cost.
A liquidity premium is charged on the FTP. Margins sum to the total spread.

name: interest_rate_risk_capital_irrbb
summary: IRRBB supervisory outlier test against Tier-1 capital.
description:
[REGULATORY] BCBS d368 §118: a bank is an outlier if the worst-case EVE
decline exceeds 15% of Tier-1 capital. Capital implied is the breach amount.

name: irrbb_internal_model
summary: Internal-model IRRBB EVE using a bank's own rate scenarios.
description:
Unlike the standardised framework this accepts an arbitrary matrix of
rate-shock scenarios (e.g. historical or Monte Carlo simulated) and reports
the EVE distribution and a 99% worst-case.

name: irrbb_six_standard_rate_shocks
summary: Construct the six BCBS d368 standard interest-rate shock curves.
description:
[REGULATORY] BCBS d368 §115. The steepener/flattener combine scaled short
and long shocks: ``steepener = −0.65·short + 0.90·long`` and
``flattener = +0.80·short − 0.60·long`` (per-tenor short/long scalars decay
as ``e^{−t/4}``).

name: irrbb_standardised_framework
summary: Standardised IRRBB EVE measure: worst ΔEVE across the six shocks.
description:
[REGULATORY] BCBS d368. ΔEVE per scenario is the change in the present value
of net banking-book cashflows under the shocked curve; the regulatory metric
is the maximum loss (most negative ΔEVE).

name: liquidity_adjusted_nii
summary: Liquidity-adjusted NII: base NII net of the liquidity-buffer carry cost.
description:
Holding a high-quality liquid-asset buffer earns ``buffer_yield`` but is
funded at ``funding_cost`` plus a ``liquidity_premium`` — usually a net
drag. Adjusted NII = base + buffer·(yield − funding − premium).

name: loan_prepayment_rate_cpr
summary: Convert between single-monthly mortality (SMM) and CPR.
description:
``CPR = 1 − (1 − SMM)^12`` and ``SMM = 1 − (1 − CPR)^{1/12}``. Provide exactly
one of the two.

name: macaulay_duration_balance_sheet
summary: Macaulay duration of a balance-sheet cashflow stream (years).

name: modified_duration_balance_sheet
summary: Modified duration of a balance-sheet position.
description:
``D_mod = D_mac / (1 + y/m)``; with continuous discounting (frequency large)
modified ≈ Macaulay.

name: nii_sensitivity_rate_shock
summary: Net interest income sensitivity to a parallel rate shock.
description:
``ΔNII ≈ (RSA − RSL) · Δrate`` where ``RSA − RSL`` is the cumulative
one-year repricing gap. A positive gap gains NII when rates rise.

name: nii_simulation_baseline
summary: Baseline (current-rate) net-interest-income projection.
description: ``NII = Σ A_i·r^A_i − Σ L_j·r^L_j`` over the projection horizon.

name: nii_simulation_stress
summary: Stressed NII under a parallel rate shock with repricing betas.
description:
Asset and liability rates reprice by ``beta · shock`` (betas capture
incomplete pass-through, especially on deposits). Returns the stressed NII
and the change versus baseline.

name: non_maturity_deposit_stability
summary: Estimate the stable (core) portion of NMDs from a balance history.
description:
Stable balance = the low percentile of the historical balance series (the
level retained with ``confidence_level`` probability); the volatile portion
is the remainder versus the current balance.

name: option_risk_irrbb
summary: Option risk: value of automatic and behavioural embedded options.
description:
[REGULATORY] BCBS d368 distinguishes automatic options (caps/floors,
prepayment options exercised optimally) from behavioural options (early
redemption, deposit withdrawal). Total option risk = sum of both.

name: pipeline_risk_measurement
summary: Pipeline risk of rate-locked mortgage commitments not yet on balance.
description:
Exposure = ``notional · pull_through``; the rate risk scales with the
rate-lock period and rate volatility (a √time vol exposure proxy).

name: prepayment_model_mortgages
summary: Project mortgage cashflows under a constant CPR prepayment assumption.
description: Higher CPR shortens the weighted-average life (WAL) of the pool.

name: repricing_gap_analysis
summary: Repricing gap per time bucket and the cumulative gap.
description: ``gap_i = RSA_i − RSL_i``; the cumulative gap drives NII sensitivity.

name: repricing_maturity_profile
summary: Allocate balances into repricing-time buckets.

name: static_gap_analysis
summary: Static (point-in-time) repricing gap assuming a frozen balance sheet.

name: structural_hedge_optimisation
summary: Optimise a structural hedge to a target equity duration.
description:
Solves for non-negative hedge notionals (bounded by per-instrument caps)
that bring the dollar-duration of the hedge as close as possible to the
target ``equity_notional · target_duration``.

name: altman_z_score_credit_scoring
summary: Altman (1968) Z-score for public manufacturers.
description:
``Z = 1.2 X1 + 1.4 X2 + 3.3 X3 + 0.6 X4 + 1.0 X5`` with X1 = WC/TA,
X2 = RE/TA, X3 = EBIT/TA, X4 = MV equity / total liabilities, X5 = sales/TA.
Zones: ``Z > 2.99`` safe, ``1.81 <= Z <= 2.99`` grey, ``Z < 1.81`` distress.

name: basel_standardised_approach_rwa
summary: Basel Standardised-Approach RWA (CRE20).
description:
``RWA = (EAD - CRM) * risk_weight``, where the supervisory risk weight is
set by the external rating / exposure class (e.g. 0% sovereign AAA, 20%
bank, 100% corporate unrated, 150% sub-investment grade). The minimum
capital is 8% of RWA.

name: capital_valuation_adjustment_kva
summary: Capital Valuation Adjustment — lifetime cost of regulatory capital.
description:
``KVA = cost_of_capital * sum_k K_k * DF_k * dt_k`` — the present value of
the shareholders' required return on the regulatory capital held against the
trade over its life.

name: cds_pricing_isda_standard
summary: ISDA-standard CDS present value (protection-buyer perspective).
description:
PV(buyer) = protection leg - premium leg, where:
  * premium leg = spread * notional * risky annuity
    (``sum_k accrual_k DF_k S_k``),
  * protection leg = LGD * notional * ``sum_k DF_k (S_{k-1} - S_k)``.
The par spread that zeroes the PV is also returned.

name: cds_spread_to_pd_conversion
summary: Credit-triangle conversion of a CDS spread to PD.
description:
Hazard ``lambda = spread / (1 - R)``; cumulative default probability to
maturity is ``PD = 1 - exp(-lambda * T)``. The annualised marginal default
rate is also returned.

name: collateral_haircut_calculation
summary: Supervisory collateral haircut under the comprehensive approach (CRE22).
description:
The adjusted collateral value is
``C_adj = C * (1 - H_c - H_fx)`` where ``H_c`` is the market-price-volatility
haircut and ``H_fx`` the currency-mismatch haircut (8% standard). The
adjusted value is floored at zero.

name: corporate_credit_scoring_model
summary: Weighted-factor corporate credit score mapped to a PD.
description:
Combines normalised factor scores (e.g. leverage, coverage, profitability,
each in ``[0, 1]`` with 1 = strongest) into a composite ``[0, 1]`` rating
strength, then maps to PD via ``PD = pd_anchor * (1 - strength)`` floored at
``pd_floor``. A perfectly strong borrower hits the floor.

name: counterparty_credit_risk_ccr_exposure
summary: Generic CCR exposure = current exposure + add-on, net of collateral.
description:
``Exposure = max(MtM - collateral, 0) + add_on``. The current exposure is
floored at zero (a counterparty owing you nothing has no replacement cost).

name: credit_concentration_risk_hhi
summary: Herfindahl-Hirschman concentration index of a credit portfolio.
description:
``HHI = sum_i (w_i)^2`` on exposure shares. HHI = 1 means a single-name
portfolio; HHI = 1/n means perfectly granular. The effective number of
independent exposures is ``1/HHI`` (the diversification score).

name: credit_default_swap_var
summary: Parametric VaR of a single-name CDS position from spread risk.
description:
The first-order MtM sensitivity to the credit spread is the spread DV01
``= notional * risky_annuity`` (per unit spread). With a normal daily spread
move of volatility ``sigma_s``, the VaR is
``z * sigma_s * sqrt(horizon) * spread_DV01``.

name: credit_portfolio_optimisation
summary: Single-period credit-portfolio weight optimisation (return vs expected loss).
description:
Maximises a mean-EL utility ``sum_i w_i (r_i - risk_aversion * EL_i)`` subject
to ``sum w = 1`` and ``0 <= w_i <= max_weight``. With these box + simplex
constraints the solution is a greedy water-filling onto the highest
risk-adjusted scores, which is the exact optimum for a linear objective.

name: credit_spread_curve_bootstrap
summary: Bootstrap a piecewise-constant hazard / survival curve from CDS spreads.
description:
Uses the credit-triangle approximation hazard ``lambda(t) = spread(t) / LGD``
on each tenor, giving survival ``S(t) = exp(-lambda * t)`` with a piecewise
hazard between consecutive tenors. This is the standard quick bootstrap;
the full ISDA bootstrap solves leg-PV = 0 per tenor (handled by
:func:`cds_pricing_isda_standard` when validating).

name: credit_stress_testing
summary: Credit stress test: multiplicative PD/LGD shocks on the loss profile.
description:
Applies a supervisory-style stress (e.g. EBA adverse scenario) by scaling
PD and LGD, clipping to ``[0, 1]``, and reports the baseline vs stressed
expected loss and the incremental impairment.

name: credit_valuation_adjustment_cva
summary: Unilateral Credit Valuation Adjustment.
description:
The market price of counterparty default risk:
``CVA = LGD * sum_k EPE_k * DF_k * (S_{k-1} - S_k)`` with LGD = 1 - R and a
flat hazard ``lambda = spread / LGD`` (credit-triangle approximation).

name: credit_var_analytical_vasicek
summary: Analytical Vasicek large-homogeneous-portfolio Credit VaR.
description:
The Vasicek (2002) asymptotic single-risk-factor loss rate at confidence q is
``L(q) = LGD * N( (N^{-1}(PD) + sqrt(rho) N^{-1}(q)) / sqrt(1-rho) )`` — the
same conditional-default formula underlying the Basel IRB charge. VaR is the
loss rate times total EAD; UL is the VaR in excess of EL.

name: credit_var_monte_carlo
summary: Monte-Carlo Credit VaR under a one-factor Gaussian copula.
description:
Simulates correlated defaults, aggregates ``LGD * EAD`` losses, and reads
the loss quantile (VaR) and the mean tail loss (ES / CVaR). Expected Loss is
the simulation mean; Unexpected Loss is ``VaR - EL`` (economic-capital
convention).

name: creditmetrics_portfolio_model
summary: Simplified CreditMetrics (two-state) portfolio loss distribution.
description:
A default/no-default reduction of J.P. Morgan's CreditMetrics: latent asset
returns are driven by a single common factor; an obligor defaults when its
return breaches ``N^{-1}(PD)``, incurring ``LGD * exposure``. The full model
uses a multi-state rating-migration matrix — handled separately by
:func:`engine.credit_scoring.ratings_migration_matrix` — but the loss tail is
dominated by the default state captured here.

name: current_exposure_method_cem
summary: Basel I/II Current Exposure Method (CEM) EAD.
description:
``EAD = max(MtM, 0) + notional * add_on_factor``. The add-on factor is the
supervisory percentage by asset class and residual maturity (e.g. 0.5% IR
< 1y, 1.5% IR 1-5y, 6% equity). CEM is superseded by SA-CCR but retained for
legacy reporting.

name: cva_sensitivity_cva_greeks
summary: CVA sensitivities — CS01 (credit delta) and exposure delta.
description:
Computes the base CVA and:
  * ``cs01``: the change in CVA for a +1 bp parallel shift in the credit
    spread (finite-difference), the dominant CVA Greek for capital and
    hedging.
  * ``exposure_delta``: sensitivity to a 1% uniform scaling of the EPE
    profile (linear, so exact = CVA * 0.01).

name: debt_valuation_adjustment_dva
summary: Debit Valuation Adjustment — the symmetric own-default benefit.
description:
DVA mirrors CVA using the *negative* expected exposure (the amount the bank
owes) and the bank's *own* credit spread. It is a gain to the reporting
entity (own default extinguishes a liability).

name: default_correlation_matrix
summary: Pairwise default correlation from asset correlations (Gaussian copula).
description:
The default correlation between two obligors is
``rho_D = (P(both default) - PD_i PD_j) / sqrt(PD_i(1-PD_i) PD_j(1-PD_j))``
where the joint default probability is the bivariate normal CDF
``Phi_2(N^{-1}(PD_i), N^{-1}(PD_j); rho_A)`` with asset correlation rho_A.

name: downturn_lgd_adjustment
summary: Basel downturn-LGD adjustment of a long-run average LGD.
description:
CRR Art. 181 requires LGD to reflect economic-downturn conditions when these
are more conservative than the long-run average. The supervisory-style
additive add-on (EBA GL) is applied as
``LGD_downturn = LGD_LR + max(0, multiplier - 1) * (1 - LGD_LR) * 0.5`` is
*not* used here; instead a transparent multiplicative scaling is applied and
clipped to ``[floor, 1]`` so the result never under-states the long-run LGD.

name: effective_epe_regulatory
summary: Basel Effective EPE (EEPE) with the non-decreasing Effective EE profile.
description:
The Effective Expected Exposure is the running maximum of EE
``EEE(t) = max(EEE(t-1), EE(t))`` (it never decreases, capturing roll-over
risk). EEPE is the time-weighted average of EEE over the first year (CRE53).
EAD = alpha * EEPE downstream.

name: expected_loss_el_computation
summary: Expected Loss ``EL = PD * LGD * EAD``.

name: expected_positive_exposure_epe
summary: Expected Positive Exposure — time-weighted average expected exposure.
description:
EPE is the time-average of the expected-exposure profile over the horizon
(CRE53): ``EPE = (1/T) * integral_0^T EE(t) dt`` approximated by the
trapezoidal rule on the supplied grid.

name: exposure_at_default_ead_calculator
summary: EAD for a revolving / committed facility via the CCF method.
description:
``EAD = drawn + CCF * undrawn``. The CCF (a.k.a. credit-conversion factor)
captures the share of the currently undrawn commitment expected to be drawn
by the time of default. Basel F-IRB uses 0.75 for unconditionally
cancellable commitments unless otherwise specified.

name: funding_valuation_adjustment_fva
summary: Funding Valuation Adjustment — cost of funding uncollateralised exposure.
description:
``FVA = funding_spread * sum_k EPE_k * DF_k * S_k * dt_k`` — the present
value of the funding-spread carry on the expected exposure over each
interval, conditional on counterparty survival.

name: ifrs_9_12_month_ecl_stage_1
summary: IFRS 9 Stage 1 (12-month) Expected Credit Loss.
description:
For Stage 1 exposures ECL uses the 12-month PD:
``ECL = PD_12m * LGD * EAD * DF``.

name: ifrs_9_lifetime_ecl_stage_2_3
summary: IFRS 9 Stage 2/3 lifetime Expected Credit Loss.
description:
Lifetime ECL sums discounted expected loss across all future periods using
the *marginal* (per-period) PD term structure:
``ECL = sum_t marginal_PD_t * LGD_t * EAD_t * DF_t``. For Stage 3 the PD is
effectively 1 in the first period (already defaulted); callers pass the
appropriate marginal-PD vector.

name: ifrs_9_scenario_weighted_ecl
summary: Probability-weighted ECL across forward-looking macro scenarios.
description:
IFRS 9 requires ECL to reflect an unbiased probability-weighted amount over
multiple scenarios (base / upside / downside):
``ECL = sum_s weight_s * ECL_s`` with weights summing to 1.

name: ifrs_9_stage_classification_pd_threshold
summary: IFRS 9 stage classification by the PD-threshold SICR rule.
description:
Stage 3 if credit-impaired (90+ days past due, the IFRS 9 rebuttable default
presumption). Otherwise Stage 2 if a significant increase in credit risk has
occurred — either the lifetime PD has risen by at least
``sicr_relative_threshold`` times origination, OR the absolute PD increase
exceeds ``sicr_absolute_threshold``. Else Stage 1.

name: ifrs_9_staging_criteria_assessment
summary: Full IFRS 9 staging assessment combining quantitative and qualitative SICR.
description:
Extends the PD-threshold rule with qualitative backstops required by IFRS 9:
forbearance and internal watchlist status force at least Stage 2, while
90+ days past due forces Stage 3. The final stage is the most severe of all
triggered criteria.

name: irb_advanced_approach_capital
summary: Basel IRB Advanced-Approach capital (CRE31).
description:
Under A-IRB the bank supplies its own PD, LGD, EAD and effective maturity.
The risk-weight function is identical to F-IRB; only the parameter sources
differ.

name: irb_foundation_approach_capital
summary: Basel IRB Foundation-Approach capital (CRE31).
description:
Under F-IRB the bank supplies its own PD but uses *supervisory* LGD: 45% for
senior unsecured and 75% for subordinated claims (CRE32). EAD and maturity
are also supervisory (M defaults to 2.5 years).

name: kmv_merton_distance_to_default
summary: Merton / KMV distance-to-default and implied PD.
description:
In the structural Merton model the firm defaults at horizon T if asset value
falls below the debt face value. The distance-to-default is
``DD = (ln(V/D) + (mu - 0.5 sigma^2) T) / (sigma sqrt(T))`` and the model PD
(expected default frequency) is ``N(-DD)``.

name: logistic_regression_pd_model
summary: Fit a logistic-regression PD model by Newton-Raphson (IRLS) MLE.
description:
Estimates ``PD = sigmoid(b0 + x·b)`` from a default indicator. A small ridge
term stabilises the Hessian on separable / collinear data. An intercept is
added automatically.

name: loss_given_default_lgd_model
summary: Workout LGD as one minus the recovery rate, net of workout costs.
description:
``LGD = 1 - (recoveries - costs) / EAD``, exposure-weighted across the
facility sample and clipped to ``[0, 1]``.

name: machine_learning_pd_calibration
summary: Platt-scaling calibration of raw ML scores into well-calibrated PDs.
description:
Many ML classifiers (gradient boosting, random forests) emit uncalibrated
scores. Platt scaling fits a one-dimensional logistic map
``PD = sigmoid(a * score + b)`` so the output is a true probability. The fit
reuses the Newton-Raphson logistic solver on the single score feature.

name: macroeconomic_overlays_ecl
summary: Apply forward-looking macroeconomic overlays to a base ECL.
description:
Adjusts ECL for projected macro deviations via a multiplicative factor
``adj = 1 + sum_j sensitivity_j * factor_j`` (clamped at 0), then adds a
discretionary management overlay. Captures the IFRS 9 requirement to
incorporate forward-looking information not in the through-the-cycle model.

name: margin_valuation_adjustment_mva
summary: Margin Valuation Adjustment — funding cost of posted initial margin.
description:
``MVA = spread * sum_k IM_k * DF_k * dt_k`` — present value of the carry on
posting (and funding) initial margin that earns less than the bank's funding
cost over the trade's life.

name: maturity_adjustment_basel_irb
summary: Basel IRB maturity adjustment (CRE31.6).
description:
``b(PD) = (0.11852 - 0.05478 ln PD)^2`` and
``MA = (1 + (M - 2.5) b) / (1 - 1.5 b)``. At M = 2.5 the adjustment is
exactly 1.0 by construction.

name: point_in_time_pd_estimation
summary: Derive a point-in-time PD from a TTC PD and a macro factor.
description:
Inverse of the TTC transform: shifts the probit-domain TTC score by a
sensitivity-scaled standardised macro index ``z`` (negative ``z`` = adverse
conditions raise the PD): ``score_PIT = N^{-1}(PD_TTC) - sensitivity * z``.

name: potential_future_exposure_pfe
summary: Potential Future Exposure profile via Monte-Carlo (arithmetic BM proxy).
description:
Simulates the netting-set value as ``V_t = V_0 + drift*t + sigma*sqrt(t)*Z``
and reports the per-step PFE (high quantile of positive exposure) and the
peak PFE. Randomness is pre-drawn in pure Python (RULE 3).

name: probability_of_default_pd_estimation
summary: Estimate PD from observed default cohorts (cohort / frequency method).
description:
Computes the per-cohort default frequency and the obligor-weighted pooled
PD, then applies the Basel regulatory floor (3 bps for non-defaulted
exposures under CRR Art. 160/163).

name: ratings_migration_matrix
summary: Estimate a row-stochastic ratings-migration matrix (cohort method).
description:
Counts observed transitions and normalises each row to a probability
distribution. Empty rows (no obligors observed in that state) are set to the
identity (a self-transition), keeping the matrix row-stochastic.

name: recovery_rate_estimation
summary: Estimate the recovery rate (1 - LGD) from a defaulted-facility sample.
description:
Supports optional present-valuing of recoveries via per-facility discount
factors (workout recoveries are received some time after default).

name: retail_scorecard_pd_model
summary: Retail scorecard: additive points to a PD via the points-to-double-odds map.
description:
A scorecard sums attribute points into a score; the score relates to odds by
``odds = base_odds * 2^{(score - base_score)/pdo}`` (PDO = points to double
the odds). PD = ``1 / (1 + odds)``.

name: sector_default_rate_analysis
summary: Per-sector default-rate analysis with a concentration of distress.
description:
Computes each sector's default rate, the obligor-weighted overall rate and
each sector's relative risk versus the portfolio average (lift > 1 means the
sector defaults more than average).

name: sme_correlation_factor_basel
summary: Basel SME firm-size correlation adjustment (CRE31.10).
description:
For SME corporate exposures (sales €5m-€50m) the asset correlation is
reduced by a size term:
``R_SME = R_corp - 0.04 * (1 - (S - 5)/45)`` with S clamped to ``[5, 50]``.
This lowers the capital charge for smaller, more idiosyncratic borrowers.

name: sovereign_credit_risk_assessment
summary: Composite sovereign credit-risk score from macro-fiscal indicators.
description:
Maps standard sovereign indicators into a ``[0, 100]`` creditworthiness
score (higher = stronger): high debt/GDP and twin deficits reduce the score;
larger FX reserves and stronger governance raise it. The score is mapped to
an indicative PD via a logistic transform.

name: standardised_approach_ccr_sa_ccr
summary: Basel SA-CCR EAD (CRE52).
description:
``EAD = alpha * (RC + PFE)`` where the replacement cost is
``RC = max(MtM - collateral, 0)`` (unmargined) and ``PFE = multiplier *
AddOn_aggregate`` with the regulatory recognition-of-excess-collateral
multiplier ``multiplier = min(1, 0.05 + 0.95 * exp((MtM - C)/(1.9 * AddOn)))``.
The supervisory ``alpha`` is 1.4.

name: through_the_cycle_pd_adjustment
summary: Convert a point-in-time PD to a through-the-cycle PD.
description:
TTC PDs dampen the macro cycle for stable regulatory capital. A convex blend
in the Gaussian-score (probit) domain is used so the result stays a valid
probability: ``score_TTC = (1-w) score_PIT + w score_LRA`` with
``w = cyclicality`` and ``score = N^{-1}(PD)``.

name: unexpected_loss_ul_computation
summary: Stand-alone Unexpected Loss per exposure and the un-diversified sum.
description:
For a Bernoulli default with deterministic LGD, the stand-alone UL of one
exposure is ``EAD * LGD * sqrt(PD(1-PD))`` — the loss standard deviation.
The portfolio UL reported here is the *sum* of stand-alone ULs (i.e. the
fully-correlated upper bound); correlation-aware UL is handled by the
Vasicek / CreditMetrics models in :mod:`engine.credit_var`.

name: wrong_way_risk_adjustment
summary: Wrong-way-risk (WWR) multiplicative adjustment to CVA.
description:
When exposure rises as the counterparty's credit deteriorates (positive
correlation), CVA is understated. A first-order alpha multiplier
``alpha = 1 + correlation * exposure_volatility`` (clamped >= 0) scales the
base CVA; negative correlation gives right-way risk (alpha < 1).

name: xva_aggregation
summary: Aggregate the XVA components into a total valuation adjustment.
description:
Sign convention (cost to the bank is positive, reducing the trade value):
``total_xva = CVA - DVA + FVA + KVA + MVA``. DVA is a benefit and so enters
negatively. The adjusted price is ``risk_free_price - total_xva`` downstream.

name: american_option_lsm
summary: American option price via Longstaff-Schwartz Monte Carlo (LSM).
description:
Allows early exercise at every time step. The price must be >= the European
price of the same option.

name: asian_option_pricer
summary: Arithmetic-average Asian option price via Monte Carlo.
description:
The averaging reduces volatility, so an Asian option is worth less than the
corresponding vanilla European option.

name: asset_swap_spread
summary: Par-par asset-swap spread.
description:
The spread equating the bond's net present value (relative to par) to an
annuity of the swap's fixed-leg PV01:
``ASW = (PV_bond − par) / annuity``, expressed in basis points.

name: barrier_option_pricer
summary: Single-barrier option price (Reiner-Rubinstein closed form).
description:
Uses the in-out parity ``knock-in + knock-out = vanilla`` so any of the four
standard combinations is supported. Rebates are not modelled (set to 0).

name: basket_option_pricer
summary: Basket option price via Monte Carlo on a weighted sum of assets.
description:
Diversification means the basket option is worth no more than the weighted
sum of single-asset options.

name: bermudan_option_pricer
summary: Bermudan option price via LSM with discrete exercise dates.
description:
Early exercise is allowed only on an evenly-spaced subset of the time grid.
Price lies between the European and American values.

name: binomial_tree_option_pricer
summary: Cox-Ross-Rubinstein binomial tree option price.
description:
Handles European and American exercise. European prices converge to
Black-Scholes as ``n_steps`` grows.

name: black_scholes_european_option
summary: Black-Scholes-Merton price of a European option.
description:
``Call = S e^{-qτ} N(d1) − K e^{-rτ} N(d2)``; the put follows by parity.
When ``tau == 0`` the intrinsic value is returned (zero-time limit) and when
``sigma == 0`` the discounted-forward intrinsic value is returned.

name: black_scholes_greeks
summary: Closed-form Black-Scholes first-order Greeks.
description:
Returns delta, gamma, vega, theta (per year) and rho. Gamma and vega are
identical for calls and puts.

name: bond_pricer_fixed_coupon
summary: Price a fixed-coupon bond by discounting its cashflows at a flat yield.
description:
Price falls as yield rises (inverse relationship), and equals par when the
coupon rate equals the yield.

name: bond_pricer_floating_rate
summary: Price a floating-rate note (FRN) from projected forward rates.
description:
Each coupon is ``(reference_rate + spread) / frequency · face``. On a reset
date with discount rates equal to the reference rates, an FRN prices near
par plus the PV of the spread.

name: bootstrap_yield_curve
summary: Bootstrap zero (spot) rates from par-coupon bond rates.
description:
Sequentially solves for each discount factor so each par bond prices to par,
then converts discount factors to continuously-compounded zero rates.

name: callable_bond_pricer
summary: Price a callable bond (issuer's option) on a short-rate binomial tree.
description:
A callable bond is worth no more than the equivalent straight bond — the
embedded call belongs to the issuer.

name: cap_floor_pricer
summary: Price an interest-rate cap/floor as a strip of caplets/floorlets.

name: caplet_floorlet_pricer_black
summary: Price a single caplet/floorlet under the Black (lognormal) model.
description:
A caplet is a call on the forward rate; a floorlet is a put. Caplet +
floorlet (same strike) replicate a payer FRA (put-call parity).

name: chooser_option_pricer
summary: Simple chooser option price (closed form).
description:
At ``tau_choose`` the holder picks call or put (same strike/expiry). By
put-call parity the value is a call plus a put on a reduced-maturity
underlying: ``C(S,K,T) + P(S, K e^{-r(T-t)}·..., t)``. Worth at least the
more valuable of the embedded call and put.

name: compound_option_pricer
summary: Compound option (option-on-option) price via nested valuation / MC.
description:
Simulates the underlying asset to the compound expiry, computes the
Black-Scholes value of the underlying option there, then discounts the
compound payoff. Supports the four standard compound types.

name: convertible_bond_pricer
summary: Price a convertible bond via the bond-floor + conversion-value maximum.
description:
Value = max(straight bond floor, conversion value), a simple but standard
lower-bound decomposition. The convertible is always worth at least its
conversion value and at least its bond floor.

name: convexity
summary: Bond convexity — the second-order yield sensitivity (always >= 0 for
description:
option-free bonds).

``C = Σ cf_k · t_k(t_k + 1/m) · (1+y/m)^{-(m t_k + 2)} / P``.

name: cox_ingersoll_ross_model
summary: CIR model: closed-form ZCB price + simulated (non-negative) short rate.
description:
``dr = κ(θ−r)dt + σ√r dW``. The square-root diffusion keeps ``r >= 0``. The
Feller condition ``2κθ ≥ σ²`` guarantees strict positivity.

name: credit_default_swap_cds_pricer
summary: Price a CDS via a flat-hazard-rate reduced-form model.
description:
Premium leg = ``spread · Σ τ · DF · Q``; protection leg =
``(1−R) · Σ DF · (Q_{i−1} − Q_i)`` with survival ``Q(t)=e^{−λt}``. The par
spread zeroes the swap value.

name: cross_currency_swap_pricer
summary: Price a fixed-fixed cross-currency swap (with notional exchange).
description:
Values each leg in its own currency (coupons + final notional), converts the
foreign leg at the FX spot, and nets. Pay-domestic = pay the domestic leg,
receive the foreign leg.

name: digital_option_pricer
summary: Cash-or-nothing digital (binary) option price.
description: ``Call = payout · e^{-rτ} N(d2)``, ``Put = payout · e^{-rτ} N(-d2)``.

name: displaced_diffusion_model
summary: Displaced-diffusion (shifted lognormal) European option price.
description:
Prices ``(S + a)`` as a lognormal with vol scaled by ``S/(S+a)`` — a simple
way to interpolate between lognormal (a=0) and normal-like dynamics. Reduces
exactly to Black-Scholes when ``displacement == 0``.

name: duration_macaulay
summary: Macaulay duration — PV-weighted average time to cashflows (in years).

name: dv01_pvbp
summary: DV01 / PVBP — price change for a 1 basis-point yield move.
description: Computed by central difference of the price function at ±0.5bp.

name: effective_duration
summary: Effective duration from re-priced bond values under a parallel shock.
description:
``D_eff = (P− − P+) / (2 · P0 · Δy)`` — model-agnostic, so it captures
embedded optionality (callable/puttable) that analytic duration misses.

name: equity_swap_pricer
summary: Value an equity swap leg (equity return vs funding).
description: ``notional · (equity_return − funding·τ) · DF`` to the equity receiver.

name: forward_rate_agreement_fra
summary: Mark-to-market value of a forward rate agreement (long = pay fixed).
description:
``Value = notional · (forward − fra_rate) · accrual · DF(end)``. Zero value
when the contracted FRA rate equals the projected forward.

name: fx_forward_pricer
summary: FX forward rate and mark-to-market via covered interest-rate parity.
description:
``F = S · e^{(r_dom − r_for)·τ}``. If a contracted forward is supplied, the
MtM value (domestic ccy) of a long-foreign position is
``notional · (F − contracted) · e^{−r_dom·τ}``.

name: fx_option_pricer_garman_kohlhagen
summary: Garman-Kohlhagen FX option price.
description:
Black-Scholes with the foreign rate acting as a continuous dividend yield:
``Call = S e^{−r_for τ} N(d1) − K e^{−r_dom τ} N(d2)``. Satisfies FX
put-call parity ``C − P = S e^{−r_for τ} − K e^{−r_dom τ}``.

name: heston_stochastic_volatility_model
summary: Heston stochastic-volatility European option price (semi-analytic).
description:
Prices via the single-integral representation using the characteristic
function. As ``sigma`` (vol-of-vol) → 0 with ``v0 = theta`` the price tends
to Black-Scholes with constant vol ``sqrt(theta)``.

name: hull_white_short_rate_model
summary: Hull-White one-factor model with a constant mean-reversion level.
description:
``dr = κ(θ−r)dt + σ dW`` — the extended-Vasicek form; with a constant θ the
closed-form ZCB price coincides with Vasicek. Returns the analytic bond
price and a Monte Carlo cross-check.

name: inflation_linked_bond_pricer
summary: Price an inflation-linked (real) bond with index-uplifted principal.
description:
Coupons and principal accrete with cumulative inflation; the resulting
nominal cashflows are discounted at the real yield (the standard
real-cashflow / real-yield convention).

name: interest_rate_swap_irs_pricer
summary: Price a vanilla fixed-vs-float interest-rate swap.
description:
Float leg PV = ``notional · Σ fwd_i · τ_i · DF_i``; fixed leg PV =
``notional · fixed · Σ τ_i · DF_i``. Swap value to the payer is
``float − fixed``. The par (break-even) fixed rate is also returned.

name: lmm_bgm_rate_model
summary: LIBOR Market Model (BGM) forward-rate Monte Carlo simulation.

name: local_volatility_dupire_model
summary: Dupire local volatility surface from a call-price surface.
description:
Uses finite differences of the Dupire equation
``σ_loc² = (∂C/∂T + r K ∂C/∂K) / (½ K² ∂²C/∂K²)`` on the supplied grid.

name: lookback_option_pricer
summary: Lookback option price via Monte Carlo.
description:
Floating-strike: call pays ``S_T − min`` (>= 0), put pays ``max − S_T``.
Fixed-strike: call pays ``max − K``, put pays ``K − min``. Always >= the
corresponding vanilla payoff.

name: modified_duration
summary: Modified duration = Macaulay duration / (1 + y/m).
description:
Approximates the percentage price change for a 1-unit yield move:
``ΔP/P ≈ −D_mod · Δy``.

name: monte_carlo_option_pricer
summary: Monte Carlo price of a European option (terminal GBM payoff).
description:
Randoms are pre-drawn in pure Python (CLAUDE.md §3.1 RULE 3); the JIT kernel
only consumes the pre-drawn standard-normal array.

name: nelson_siegel_curve_fit
summary: Fit a Nelson-Siegel curve to observed yields.
description:
Parameters: ``beta0`` (level), ``beta1`` (slope), ``beta2`` (curvature),
``tau`` (decay). ``beta0 + beta1`` is the instantaneous short rate and
``beta0`` is the asymptotic long rate.

name: nelson_siegel_svensson_curve
summary: Fit the Nelson-Siegel-Svensson (six-parameter) curve.
description:
Adds a second curvature hump (``beta3``, ``tau2``) to Nelson-Siegel, giving
a closer fit to longer/more complex term structures.

name: normal_inverse_gaussian_model
summary: Normal Inverse Gaussian European option price via Monte Carlo.
description:
NIG is Brownian motion subordinated by an inverse-Gaussian process. The
drift is corrected so the discounted spot is a martingale.

name: oas_option_adjusted_spread
summary: Option-adjusted spread of a callable bond.
description:
Finds the constant spread added to the short rate on the pricing tree that
reprices the callable bond to its market price — stripping out the embedded
option so spreads are comparable across bonds.

name: ois_curve_sonia_sofr
summary: Build an OIS (SONIA/SOFR) discount curve from quoted OIS swap rates.
description:
OIS swaps pay annually against compounded overnight; the discount curve is
bootstrapped exactly as for par swaps (single-curve OIS-discounting).

name: overnight_index_swap_ois
summary: Value a single-period overnight index swap.
description:
Net cashflow = ``notional · (compounded_overnight − fixed) · accrual``,
discounted. Zero value when the compounded rate equals the fixed rate.

name: puttable_bond_pricer
summary: Price a puttable bond (holder's option) on a short-rate binomial tree.
description:
A puttable bond is worth at least the equivalent straight bond — the
embedded put belongs to the holder.

name: rainbow_option_pricer
summary: Rainbow (best-of / worst-of) option price via Monte Carlo.
description:
Payoff references the max (best-of) or min (worst-of) of the terminal asset
prices against the strike.

name: rough_volatility_rbergomi_model
summary: Rough Bergomi (rBergomi) European option price via Monte Carlo.
description:
A rough-volatility model with Hurst exponent ``H < 0.5``. Randoms are
pre-drawn in pure Python (CLAUDE.md §3.1 RULE 3).

name: sabr_volatility_model
summary: SABR implied (lognormal/Black) volatility via Hagan's expansion.
description:
Returns the Black implied volatility for the given strike under the SABR
dynamics. At-the-money it reduces to the well-known ATM SABR vol.

name: spread_option_kirk_approximation
summary: Spread option price via Kirk's approximation.
description:
Prices an option on ``S1 − S2`` by reducing it to a Black-76 option on the
ratio with an effective volatility. Exact when ``strike == 0`` (Margrabe).
Inputs are treated as forwards (Black-76); the value is discounted once.

name: swap_rate_curve
summary: Par swap rates implied by a discount-factor curve.
description:
For each tenor, ``swap_rate = (1 − DF(T)) / (Σ τ · DF)`` — the fixed rate
that makes a par swap have zero value.

name: swaption_pricer_black
summary: Price a European swaption under the Black model.
description:
``Price = annuity · Black(forward_swap_rate, strike, vol, expiry)``. A payer
swaption is a call on the swap rate; a receiver swaption is a put.

name: swaption_pricer_sabr
summary: Price a swaption using a SABR-implied Black volatility.
description:
Computes the SABR lognormal vol for the (forward, strike, expiry) point via
Hagan's expansion, then plugs it into the Black swaption formula.

name: total_return_swap_trs
summary: Value a total-return swap leg.
description:
The total-return receiver gets the asset's total return and pays a financing
rate (e.g. SOFR + spread): ``notional · (asset_return − financing·τ) · DF``.

name: trinomial_tree_option_pricer
summary: Boyle trinomial tree option price.
description:
Up/middle/down branching converges to Black-Scholes for European options.
Handles American exercise.

name: variance_gamma_model
summary: Variance Gamma European option price via Monte Carlo.
description:
Time-changes Brownian motion by a Gamma subordinator (mean 1, variance
``nu``). The martingale drift correction ``omega`` is computed in closed
form so the discounted spot is a martingale.

name: vasicek_interest_rate_model
summary: Vasicek model: closed-form zero-coupon bond price + simulated short rate.
description:
``dr = κ(θ−r)dt + σ dW``. The affine ZCB price is ``P = A·e^{−B·r0}``. The
short rate is Gaussian (can go negative).

name: yield_to_call
summary: Yield to call — yield assuming redemption at the first call date.
description:
Builds the cashflow stream truncated at ``call_date`` with redemption at
``call_price`` and solves for the yield.

name: yield_to_maturity
summary: Yield to maturity — the flat rate that discounts cashflows to ``price``.
description:
Solved by Brent root-finding. Recovers the input yield exactly when ``price``
was produced by :func:`engine.deriv_bonds.bond_pricer_fixed_coupon`.

name: z_spread_calculator
summary: Z-spread — constant spread over the zero curve that reprices the bond.
description: Solves for ``z`` such that ``Σ cf_k (1 + (zero_k + z)/m)^{-m t_k} = price``.

name: zero_coupon_bond_pricer
summary: Price a zero-coupon bond: ``face / (1 + y/m)^{m·T}``.

name: asset_encumbrance_ratio
summary: Asset encumbrance ratio (EBA reporting).
description:
``encumbrance = encumbered assets / total assets``. High encumbrance reduces
the unencumbered asset pool available to monetise in stress.

name: available_stable_funding_asf_calc
summary: Available Stable Funding for the NSFR numerator.
description:
ASF is the weighted sum of funding sources by their ASF factor. Basel III
assigns higher factors to more stable funding (e.g. capital and >1y funding
= 100%, stable retail deposits = 95%, less-stable = 90%, wholesale <1y
typically 50% or 0%).

name: cash_flow_ladder_1_year
summary: One-year bucketed contractual cash-flow ladder.
description:
Aggregates inflows and outflows into the standard maturity buckets and
computes the per-bucket and cumulative liquidity gap.

name: cash_flow_ladder_30_day
summary: 30-day daily contractual cash-flow ladder.
description:
Projects the daily net and cumulative liquidity position over a 30-day
horizon. The minimum cumulative balance (including the opening balance) is
the tightest liquidity point — if negative the institution faces a funding
shortfall on that day.

name: central_bank_facility_eligibility
summary: Central-bank facility collateral eligibility and borrowing capacity.
description:
Filters assets meeting the central bank's minimum credit rating (encoded as
an ordinal where higher = better) and computes the post-central-bank-haircut
borrowing capacity from eligible assets.

name: collateral_availability_analysis
summary: Collateral availability — post-haircut monetisable value.
description:
Computes the net realisable collateral value after haircuts and netting off
already-pledged amounts — the counterbalancing capacity available to raise
secured funding.

name: combined_stress_scenario
summary: Combined idiosyncratic + market-wide stress scenario.
description:
The Basel/EBA reference scenario: a firm-specific shock occurring inside a
market-wide crisis. Liability run-off is aggravated (retail default 15%,
wholesale 100%) *and* HQLA value is reduced by stressed market haircuts.

name: contingency_funding_plan_trigger
summary: Evaluate Contingency Funding Plan (CFP) activation triggers.
description:
Compares current early-warning metrics against their activation thresholds.
A metric breaches when its value falls *below* the threshold (lower = worse;
e.g. LCR, survival days). Returns the list of breached triggers and the CFP
activation decision.

name: contingent_liquidity_risk
summary: Contingent liquidity risk from undrawn commitments and guarantees.
description:
Estimates the expected contingent outflow as ``commitment * draw_probability
* credit-conversion-factor`` — the liquidity that off-balance-sheet
commitments (undrawn lines, guarantees) could absorb in stress.

name: cross_currency_liquidity_bridge
summary: Cross-currency liquidity bridge via FX swap.
description:
Sizes the FX swap needed to fund a shortfall in one currency using surplus
in another. ``fx_rate`` converts one unit of the surplus currency into the
shortfall currency; a ``swap_haircut`` reduces the usable surplus to reflect
swap-market stress.

name: deposit_stability_classification
summary: Classify deposits as stable vs less-stable from a stability score.
description:
Each deposit carries a stability score in [0, 1] (e.g. derived from
insurance coverage, transactional relationship, tenor). Deposits at or above
``stable_threshold`` are classified stable (lower LCR run-off), the rest
less-stable.

name: early_warning_indicator_liquidity
summary: Liquidity early-warning indicator (EWI) dashboard.
description:
Evaluates each EWI against its threshold and a per-indicator direction
(``"higher_breach"`` means a value above threshold is a warning, e.g. funding
spread; ``"lower_breach"`` means below threshold is a warning, e.g. LCR). The
aggregate signal escalates with the number of triggered indicators.

name: funding_cost_analysis
summary: Weighted-average funding cost.
description:
Computes the amount-weighted average cost of the funding base and the total
annual funding cost in currency terms.

name: funding_tenor_analysis
summary: Weighted-average funding tenor and short-term reliance.
description:
Computes the amount-weighted average tenor of the funding base and the
proportion of funding maturing within 90 days — a core ILAAP structural
metric (longer WAL == more stable funding).

name: fx_liquidity_risk_by_currency
summary: FX liquidity risk — net position per significant currency.
description:
Computes the net liquidity gap in each currency (inflows - outflows). A
significant negative position signals reliance on FX swap markets to fund
the shortfall — a key vulnerability if swap markets seize.

name: hqla_level_1_asset_classifier
summary: Classify and value Level 1 HQLA.
description:
Level 1 assets (cash, central-bank reserves, 0%-risk-weight sovereign debt)
receive a 0% haircut by default and have no composition cap (BCBS 238 §50).

name: hqla_level_2a_asset_classifier
summary: Classify and value Level 2A HQLA.
description:
Level 2A assets (20%-risk-weight sovereigns, certain covered bonds, high-
grade corporates) carry a minimum 15% haircut (BCBS 238 §52).

name: hqla_level_2b_asset_classifier
summary: Classify and value Level 2B HQLA.
description:
Level 2B assets (RMBS 25% haircut, lower-grade corporates and qualifying
equities 50% haircut) carry a minimum 25% haircut (BCBS 238 §54).

name: idiosyncratic_stress_scenario
summary: Idiosyncratic (name-specific) stress scenario.
description:
Models a firm-specific crisis (e.g. rating downgrade): partial retail
deposit flight and complete loss of wholesale funding rollover. Wholesale
run-off defaults to 100% — the hallmark of a name-specific shock.

name: ilaap_internal_liquidity_metric
summary: ILAAP internal liquidity adequacy metric.
description:
Combines the institution's own counterbalancing-capacity coverage ratio
(CBC / stressed outflow) with the survival-horizon adequacy versus the
internal minimum (commonly 90 days). Both must hold for internal adequacy.

name: ilaap_stress_testing_framework
summary: ILAAP stress-testing framework aggregator.
description:
Aggregates the outcomes of multiple named liquidity stress scenarios into an
ILAAP-style summary: the binding (worst) scenario, the count of scenarios
breached, and overall adequacy. Each scenario value must expose a
``surplus_deficit`` figure (as produced by the scenario functions above).

name: intraday_liquidity_monitor
summary: Intraday liquidity monitor (BCBS 248).
description:
Tracks the intraday liquidity position from time-stamped net payment flows
and reports the peak usage (largest negative intraday position relative to
the opening balance) and the largest net debit position — the BCBS 248
monitoring tools.

name: intraday_liquidity_stress_test
summary: Intraday liquidity stress test (BCBS 248 stress scenarios).
description:
Stresses the intraday profile by delaying a fraction of *inflows* (positive
flows): a ``delay_factor`` of expected inflows is removed from the intraday
path, sharpening the peak liquidity requirement. Reports the stressed peak
usage and whether the opening buffer plus any additional shock survives.

name: intragroup_liquidity_flow
summary: Intragroup liquidity flow netting.
description:
Nets bilateral liquidity positions across group entities to derive each
entity's net provider/receiver status and the total internal liquidity
transferred. Positive = net provider of liquidity to the group.

name: liquidity_buffer_sizing
summary: Size the liquidity buffer to the peak cumulative stressed outflow.
description:
The required buffer equals the maximum cumulative net outflow over the
stress horizon (the deepest point of the cash-flow trough), optionally
uplifted by a management ``confidence_buffer`` margin.

name: liquidity_coverage_ratio_lcr
summary: Basel III Liquidity Coverage Ratio.
description:
``LCR = HQLA / net 30-day outflows`` where net outflows are gross outflows
minus *capped* inflows. Recognised inflows are floored at ``inflow_cap`` of
gross outflows (default 75%), guaranteeing net outflows never fall below
25% of gross — the BCBS 238 §69 cap.

name: liquidity_gap_analysis
summary: Maturity-bucket liquidity gap (assets vs liabilities).
description:
Computes the structural maturity mismatch: ``gap_i = assets_i -
liabilities_i`` per bucket, plus the cumulative gap. A positive cumulative
gap means more assets than liabilities mature by that point (a funding
surplus); a negative gap signals a refinancing need.

name: liquidity_risk_appetite_threshold
summary: Map a liquidity metric to a RAG (red/amber/green) risk-appetite zone.
description:
For ``higher_is_better`` metrics (LCR, NSFR, survival days) green is at or
above ``green_threshold`` and red below ``amber_threshold``. For
lower-is-better metrics (e.g. funding concentration) the comparison inverts.

name: liquidity_scorecard_aggregation
summary: Weighted liquidity scorecard aggregation.
description:
Combines individual liquidity metric scores (each typically 0-100) into a
single weighted composite score and maps it to a RAG rating.

name: liquidity_stress_scenario
summary: Generic single liquidity stress scenario.
description:
Applies category-specific run-off rates to funding balances to derive
stressed outflows, nets inflows, and tests whether HQLA covers the net
stressed outflow.

name: liquidity_transfer_pricing
summary: Liquidity Transfer Pricing (LTP) charge for a funding position.
description:
The FTP charge passes the cost of liquidity to business lines: the all-in
transfer rate is ``base_rate + term liquidity premium + contingent liquidity
premium``. The annual charge is that rate applied to notional; the lifetime
charge multiplies by tenor.

name: liquidity_var_liqvar
summary: Liquidity VaR (LiqVaR) by Monte Carlo simulation of stressed net outflows.
description:
Simulates the distribution of stressed net cash outflows as
``base_outflow * (1 + vol * Z)`` and reads the loss quantile at the
confidence level. LiqVaR is the outflow level not exceeded with the given
confidence — the liquidity analogue of market VaR.

Per CLAUDE.md §3.1 RULE 3 the N(0,1) shocks are pre-drawn in pure Python and
passed to the JIT kernel; an analytic normal quantile is also returned for
validation.

name: market_wide_stress_scenario
summary: Market-wide stress scenario.
description:
Models a system-wide crisis where HQLA monetisation value falls due to
widened market haircuts (flight to quality, fire-sale discounts). Outflows
are met from the haircut-reduced HQLA value.

name: net_stable_funding_ratio_nsfr
summary: Basel III Net Stable Funding Ratio.
description:
``NSFR = ASF / RSF`` and must be >= 100% (BCBS 295). Measures the proportion
of long-term assets funded by stable funding sources over a one-year horizon.

name: repo_market_stress_haircut
summary: Repo market stress — incremental margin call from widened haircuts.
description:
Under stress, repo haircuts widen by a multiplier. The incremental margin
requirement is the extra collateral (or cash) the institution must post to
maintain the same secured borrowing.

name: required_stable_funding_rsf_calc
summary: Required Stable Funding for the NSFR denominator.
description:
RSF is the weighted sum of assets by their RSF factor. More liquid / shorter
assets attract lower factors (Level 1 HQLA = 5%, Level 2A = 15%, loans = 50-
85%, illiquid assets = 100%).

name: retail_deposit_runoff_rate
summary: Aggregate retail deposit run-off (Basel LCR categories).
description:
Computes the blended run-off rate across retail deposit categories (e.g.
stable 5%, less-stable 10%, non-operational higher) and the total expected
30-day run-off amount.

name: secured_funding_rollover_risk
summary: Secured funding (repo) rollover risk.
description:
Estimates the funding gap from secured transactions that fail to roll: the
non-rolled portion of each maturing tranche must be replaced or repaid.

name: survival_horizon_calculator
summary: Survival horizon — days until cumulative net outflow exhausts HQLA.
description:
Walks forward through the daily net-outflow path subtracting from the HQLA
counterbalancing capacity. The survival horizon is the last day on which the
remaining buffer is still non-negative.

name: wholesale_funding_concentration
summary: Wholesale funding concentration via the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index.
description:
Computes the HHI of funding shares across counterparties (sum of squared
shares, in [1/n, 1]) plus the largest single-counterparty share. Higher HHI
means more concentrated, less diversified funding.

name: basel_capital_addon_multiplier
summary: Basel capital add-on multiplier from the backtest breach count.
description:
Green zone (< 5 breaches) → 3.0; yellow zone (5-9) → the BCBS graduated
schedule (3.40 .. 3.85); red zone (>= 10) → 4.0. These values are set by the
Basel Committee (CLAUDE.md §4.3).

name: charm_delta_decay
summary: Charm — sensitivity of delta to time to maturity (∂Δ/∂τ).
description:
Computed in the time-to-maturity convention so that a finite-difference of
delta with respect to τ reproduces this value.

name: christoffersen_independence_test
summary: Christoffersen independence (clustering) test.
description:
Likelihood-ratio test that breaches are serially independent (no
clustering), via a first-order Markov transition model. Chi-squared with
1 dof at the 95% critical value.

name: combined_backtesting
summary: Combined (conditional coverage) backtest: Kupiec + Christoffersen.
description:
The Christoffersen conditional-coverage statistic ``LR_cc = LR_POF + LR_ind``
is chi-squared with 2 dof, tested at the 95% critical value. It rejects a
model that either mis-counts or clusters its breaches.

name: component_var
summary: Component VaR via Euler allocation.
description:
Allocates total VaR to each position as ``w_i * marginal_i``. Because VaR is
homogeneous of degree 1 in the weights, the components sum exactly to the
total VaR (Euler's theorem) — the property regulators require for a
coherent risk decomposition.

name: compute_breaches
summary: Backtesting: count days where actual loss exceeded VaR estimate.
description:
Basel traffic-light zones:
  Green  < 5 breaches / 250 days
  Yellow 5-9 breaches
  Red    >= 10 breaches

name: compute_cvar
summary: Conditional VaR (Expected Shortfall) — mean of losses beyond VaR threshold.
description: Regulatory standard under Basel III / FRTB for market risk capital.

name: compute_loss_percentiles
summary: Returns a dict of {percentile_label: loss_value} for fan chart display.
description: Default percentiles cover the standard regulatory range.

name: compute_rolling_var
summary: Parametric (Gaussian) rolling VaR using a expanding window.
description:
Fast approximation for backtesting — not the full Monte Carlo.
Uses scipy.stats.norm for the quantile function.

Returns array of VaR estimates, same length as returns (NaN for first window obs).

name: conditional_var_es
summary: Conditional VaR (Expected Shortfall) from a return series.
description:
The FRTB IMA capital metric is ES at 97.5% (hence the default). ES is the
mean loss conditional on exceeding the VaR threshold and is always >= VaR.

name: contagion_stress_scenario
summary: Propagate an initial shock through a contagion (spillover) network.
description:
Each round, the current shock spills to connected nodes via the contagion
matrix C; the cumulative shock is ``shock + C·shock + C²·shock + ...`` over
the requested rounds — a truncated Neumann series of the spillover operator.

name: cornish_fisher_var
summary: Cornish-Fisher (modified) VaR.
description:
Expands the Gaussian quantile with the third and fourth moments so the VaR
reflects skewness and fat tails. When skewness and excess kurtosis are both
zero it collapses exactly to the parametric delta-normal VaR.

name: correlation_matrix_historical
summary: Historical (Pearson) correlation matrix of asset returns.

name: credit_pnl_attribution
summary: Credit P&L attribution by issuer / curve.
description: Total credit P&L = Σ cs01_i · dspread_bp_i, additive across credit names.

name: cs01_credit_spread
summary: CS01 — sensitivity of a risky cashflow stream to a +1bp credit spread move.
description:
Cashflows are discounted at ``r + s``; CS01 is
``Σ cf_k · t_k · e^{-(r+s) t_k} · 1e-4`` — the price drop for a 1bp widening
of the credit spread.

name: cvar_decomposition_euler
summary: Euler decomposition of Gaussian Expected Shortfall.
description:
Under the normal model ES = sigma_p * φ(z) / (1 − α). ES is homogeneous of
degree 1 in the weights, so component ES_i = w_i * (Σ w)_i / sigma_p *
φ(z)/(1 − α) and the components sum exactly to total ES (Euler's theorem).

name: dcc_garch_dynamic_correlation
summary: DCC-GARCH dynamic conditional correlation (Engle 2002), terminal R_T.
description:
Standardises each series, then evolves the quasi-correlation
``Q_t = (1−a−b) Q̄ + a z_{t-1} z_{t-1}' + b Q_{t-1}`` and normalises to a
correlation matrix. With ``a = b = 0`` it collapses to the constant
unconditional correlation Q̄.

name: dv01_pv01_bucketed
summary: Tenor-bucketed DV01 / PV01 of a fixed cashflow stream.
description:
For continuously-discounted cashflows ``PV = Σ cf_k e^{-y t_k}`` the DV01 of
each cashflow (price change for a +1bp yield move) is
``cf_k · t_k · e^{-y t_k} · 1e-4``. Cashflows are summed into tenor buckets;
the bucket DV01s sum exactly to the total.

name: egarch_volatility_model
summary: EGARCH(1,1) asymmetric volatility model (Nelson 1991).
description:
Models log-variance, so conditional variance is positive for any parameters.
The leverage term ``gamma`` makes negative shocks raise volatility more than
positive shocks of equal size (when ``gamma < 0``).

name: es_at_multiple_confidence_levels
summary: Expected Shortfall evaluated at several confidence levels at once.
description:
Useful for limit dashboards that report internal (95%), FRTB (97.5%) and
Basel (99%) ES side by side. ES is monotone non-decreasing in confidence.

name: expected_shortfall_contribution
summary: Per-asset ES contribution by conditional expectation in the tail.
description:
Each asset's ES contribution is its average loss across exactly the
scenarios where the *portfolio* breaches VaR. By construction the
contributions sum to total ES (the additive allocation FRTB expects).

name: extreme_value_theory_var
summary: Extreme Value Theory VaR via Peaks-Over-Threshold (Generalised Pareto).
description:
Fits a Generalised Pareto Distribution to losses exceeding a high threshold
u and reads the tail quantile::

    VaR_p = u + (β/ξ) · [ ((n/N_u)(1−p))^{−ξ} − 1 ]

capturing tail behaviour beyond the empirical sample range.

name: filtered_historical_simulation_var
summary: Filtered Historical Simulation VaR (Barone-Adesi & Giannopoulos).
description:
Standardises returns by their EWMA conditional volatility, then re-scales
the standardised residuals by the *current* volatility forecast before
taking the empirical quantile. This captures volatility clustering that
plain historical simulation ignores.

name: frtb_ima_aggregate_capital_charge
summary: FRTB IMA aggregate capital charge.
description:
Combines the internally-modelled capital charge (IMCC, from ES), the
non-modellable SES add-on, and the default risk charge (MAR33.43):
``ACC = IMCC + SES + DRC``.

name: frtb_ima_expected_shortfall
summary: FRTB IMA Expected Shortfall (the regulatory ES at 97.5%).
description:
ES is the mean loss beyond the VaR threshold at the FRTB confidence of
97.5% (CLAUDE.md §4.2) and is always >= VaR.

name: frtb_ima_non_modellable_risk_factors
display_name: FRTB IMA Non Modellable Risk Factors
summary: FRTB IMA non-modellable risk factor (NMRF) capital — aggregate SES.
description:
Aggregates per-factor stressed capital add-ons (ISES) as
``SES = sqrt( (ρ·Σ ISES)² + (1−ρ²)·Σ ISES² )`` (MAR33.16). With ρ = 0 this is
the Euclidean sum; with ρ = 1 it is the linear (fully correlated) sum.

name: frtb_ima_stressed_period_finder
summary: Locate the FRTB IMA stressed period — the worst 250-day ES window.
description:
FRTB calibrates the stressed ES to the historical window of greatest stress.
This slides a 250-day window and returns the start index whose Expected
Shortfall is largest.

name: frtb_sa_default_risk_charge
summary: FRTB SA Default Risk Charge (DRC) with the hedge-benefit ratio.
description:
Net jump-to-default per issuer is risk-weighted; the gross short charge is
scaled by the Weighted-to-Short (hedge benefit) ratio
``WtS = Σ netLong / (Σ netLong + Σ|netShort|)`` (MAR22). DRC is floored at 0.

name: frtb_sa_residual_risk_addon
summary: FRTB SA Residual Risk Add-On (RRAO).
description:
A simple notional-based add-on for instruments with residual risks not
captured by the SBM: ``RRAO = Σ notional_i · weight_i`` (MAR23, e.g. 1.0% on
exotic underlyings, 0.1% otherwise).

name: frtb_sa_sensitivity_based_method
summary: FRTB SA Sensitivities-Based Method (delta) risk charge.
description:
Within each bucket the risk position is
``Kb = sqrt(Σ WS_i² + Σ_{i≠j} ρ·WS_i·WS_j)``; the charge aggregates buckets
as ``sqrt(Σ Kb² + Σ_{b≠c} γ·S_b·S_c)`` with ``S_b = Σ_i WS_i`` (MAR21).

name: fx_pnl_attribution
summary: FX P&L attribution across currency pairs.
description: Total FX P&L = Σ fx_delta_i · dFX_i, additive across currencies.

name: gamma_cross_gamma_matrix
summary: Assemble the portfolio gamma / cross-gamma matrix.
description:
The diagonal holds each underlying's net gamma (∂²V/∂S_i²); off-diagonals
hold cross-gammas (∂²V/∂S_i∂S_j). The matrix is symmetric (Schwarz's
theorem) — gamma P&L for a shock vector ds is ``0.5 · ds' G ds``.

name: gamma_pnl_attribution
summary: Gamma (convexity) P&L component: ``½ · Γ · dS²``.

name: garch_11_volatility_forecast
summary: GARCH(1,1) conditional-volatility filter and multi-step forecast.
description:
Filters the conditional variance and projects it forward. The h-step
forecast mean-reverts to the long-run variance ``ω/(1−α−β)`` at rate
``(α+β)`` — the defining property of a stationary GARCH(1,1). If ``omega`` is
not supplied it is set by variance targeting, ``ω = (1−α−β)·Var(returns)``.

name: gjr_garch_asymmetric_model
summary: GJR-GARCH(1,1) asymmetric volatility model (Glosten-Jagannathan-Runkle).
description:
A leverage indicator adds ``gamma`` to the ARCH coefficient when the prior
shock was negative, so (for ``gamma > 0``) downside shocks raise volatility
more. The long-run variance is ``ω/(1 − α − β − γ/2)``.

name: greeks_based_pnl_explain
summary: Second-order Greeks P&L explain.
description:
Predicted P&L = Δ·dS + ½Γ·dS² + ν·dσ + Θ·dt + ρ·dr. The unexplained residual
is ``actual_pnl − predicted`` — the quantity the FRTB PAT scrutinises.

name: historical_expected_shortfall
summary: Non-parametric historical Expected Shortfall.
description:
Identical tail-mean definition as :func:`conditional_var_es` but framed as
the historical-simulation ES: no distributional assumption, the empirical
tail is averaged directly.

name: historical_scenario_replay
summary: Replay historical factor moves against the current portfolio.
description:
Applies each historical day's factor returns to the current exposures and
reports the resulting P&L path, identifying the single worst day.

name: historical_simulation_var
summary: Non-parametric Historical Simulation VaR.
description:
Re-prices the portfolio under each observed historical return and reads the
empirical loss quantile — making no distributional assumption.

name: hypothetical_multi_factor_scenario
summary: P&L under a single hypothetical multi-factor shock.
description:
First-order P&L = Σ exposure_i * shock_i. Used for ad-hoc "what if" scenarios
such as a simultaneous equity sell-off and rates spike.

name: incremental_var
summary: Incremental VaR of a single position.
description:
The exact (non-marginal) effect of a position on portfolio VaR:
``VaR(full) − VaR(portfolio with position i removed)``.

name: kupiec_pof_test
summary: Kupiec Proportion-of-Failures (POF) unconditional coverage test.

name: liquidity_adjusted_es
summary: Liquidity-adjusted Expected Shortfall (FRTB IMA, MAR33.12).
description:
Scales the base-horizon ES up for risk factors that take longer than the
base liquidity horizon T to unwind::

    ES = sqrt( ES_base^2 + Σ_{j>=2} ( ES_j * sqrt((LH_j − LH_{j-1}) / T) )^2 )

where ``ES_base`` is the whole-portfolio ES at horizon T, and ``ES_j`` is the
ES with respect to factors in liquidity bucket j and longer.

name: macro_scenario_generator
summary: Generate correlated macro factor scenarios via the Cholesky factor.
description:
Draws standard-normal innovations in pure Python (CLAUDE.md §3.1 RULE 3) and
colours them with the Cholesky factor of the supplied covariance so the
generated scenarios reproduce the target factor correlation structure.

name: marginal_var
summary: Marginal VaR — sensitivity of portfolio VaR to each position weight.
description:
For the delta-normal model VaR = z * sqrt(w' Σ w), the marginal VaR is the
gradient ``∂VaR/∂w_i = z * (Σ w)_i / sigma_p``.

name: monte_carlo_expected_shortfall
summary: Monte Carlo Expected Shortfall.
description:
Runs the parametric-normal Monte Carlo engine and reads the ES (CVaR) from
the simulated loss distribution. Deterministic for a fixed seed.

name: parametric_delta_normal_var
summary: Variance-covariance (delta-normal) VaR.
description:
Assumes asset returns are jointly normal so portfolio loss is normal with
standard deviation ``sqrt(w' Σ w)``. VaR is the scaled normal quantile.

name: pnl_attribution_test_frtb_pat
summary: FRTB P&L Attribution Test (PAT) — Spearman correlation and ratio test.
description:
Jointly evaluates the Spearman rank correlation between risk-theoretical P&L
(RTPL) and hypothetical P&L (HPL) and the volatility ratio
``std(RTPL)/std(HPL)``, assigning the Basel traffic-light zone. These
thresholds are set by the Basel Committee and are not parameterised.

name: portfolio_delta_aggregated
summary: Aggregate per-position deltas into a net portfolio delta.
description:
Net delta = Σ delta_i * quantity_i. When spot prices are supplied the
cash (dollar) delta Σ delta_i * quantity_i * spot_i is also returned.

name: rates_pnl_attribution
summary: Interest-rate P&L attribution by key-rate tenor.
description:
Total rates P&L = Σ sensitivity_t · dyield_bp_t, where each sensitivity is
P&L per +1bp move at that tenor. Additive across the key-rate ladder.

name: realised_volatility
summary: Realised volatility from a block of (typically high-frequency) returns.
description:
Realised variance is the sum of squared returns; realised volatility is its
square root, and the annualised figure scales by ``sqrt(annualisation_factor)``.

name: residual_pnl_unexplained
summary: Unexplained (residual) P&L.
description:
Residual = actual P&L − Σ explained components. The residual plus the sum of
explained components reconstructs the actual P&L exactly; a large residual
relative to actual P&L flags model incompleteness (an FRTB PAT concern).

name: reverse_stress_testing
summary: Reverse stress test — find the most plausible scenario causing a target loss.
description:
Among all factor shocks producing the given loss, the most plausible (lowest
Mahalanobis magnitude under the factor covariance) lies along ``-Σ e``. The
closed-form solution for loss L is ``s* = -(L / e'Σe) · Σ e`` with magnitude
``m = L / sqrt(e'Σe)``.

name: rho_interest_rate
summary: Black-Scholes Rho — option value sensitivity to the interest rate.
description: ``Rho_call = K τ e^{-rτ} N(d2)``; ``Rho_put = -K τ e^{-rτ} N(-d2)``.

name: risk_factor_pca_decomposition
summary: Principal-component decomposition of the risk-factor covariance.
description:
Eigen-decomposes the factor covariance matrix and orders components by
descending variance. The explained-variance ratios sum to 1 (over all
components) and the eigenvalues are non-negative (covariance is PSD).

name: rolling_var_backtest
summary: Rolling-window VaR backtest over the Basel 250-day window.
description:
Estimates parametric VaR on each trailing window and counts breaches of the
realised next-day return, returning the Basel traffic-light zone.

name: sector_stress_scenario
summary: Sector-level stress scenario.
description:
Applies a shock to each sector's net exposure and aggregates. Total P&L is
the exact sum of per-sector P&L (additivity by construction).

name: sensitivity_stress_profile
summary: One-factor sensitivity stress profile.
description:
Sweeps a single risk factor across a grid of shocks (holding others flat)
and returns the P&L profile — the building block of a stress "ladder".

name: spectral_risk_measure
summary: Spectral risk measure with an exponential risk-aversion spectrum.
description:
A coherent risk measure that integrates the loss quantile against a
decreasing risk-spectrum ``φ(p) = k·e^{−k(1−p)} / (1−e^{−k})``, placing more
weight on the tail as the risk aversion k rises. SRM >= the mean loss and is
increasing in k.

name: stressed_expected_shortfall
summary: Stressed Expected Shortfall (FRTB IMA).
description:
FRTB requires ES to be calibrated to a historical period of significant
financial stress. This computes ES over the supplied stressed window
``returns[stress_start:stress_end]`` only.

name: theta_carry_attribution
summary: Theta / carry attribution.
description:
Isolates the deterministic time-decay (carry) component of P&L,
``theta · dt``, optionally net of a funding cost over the same period.

name: theta_time_decay
summary: Black-Scholes Theta — calendar time decay (∂V/∂calendar = −∂V/∂τ), per year.

name: traffic_light_backtesting
summary: Basel traffic-light backtest over the 250-day window.
description:
Counts VaR breaches and assigns the Basel zone: green (< 5 breaches), yellow
(5-9), red (>= 10). These boundaries are set by the Basel Committee.

name: vanna_delta_vega_cross
summary: Vanna — cross sensitivity ∂vega/∂S = ∂Δ/∂σ.
description:
``Vanna = −e^{-qτ} · φ(d1) · d2 / σ``. Identical for calls and puts. It
measures how delta drifts as volatility moves (and vice versa).

name: var_breach_cluster_analysis
summary: Analyse the clustering of VaR breaches.
description:
Reports the number of breach clusters (maximal runs of consecutive
breaches), the longest run, and the mean run length — diagnostics for the
independence assumption that the Christoffersen test formalises.

name: var_by_risk_factor
summary: Decompose VaR across systematic risk factors (Euler allocation).
description:
Identical Euler decomposition to :func:`component_var` but expressed in
risk-factor space: given portfolio factor exposures ``b`` and factor
covariance ``F``, the factor contribution is
``z * b_i * (F b)_i / sigma_p`` and contributions sum to the total VaR.

name: var_fan_chart
summary: VaR fan chart — parametric VaR bands across confidence levels and horizons.
description:
Produces, for each confidence level, the VaR projected over 1..H days using
square-root-of-time volatility scaling — the standard visualisation of how
the loss envelope widens with the holding period.

name: vega_pnl_attribution
summary: Vega P&L component: ``ν · dσ``.

name: vega_surface_bucketed
summary: Aggregate option vegas onto a bucketed (expiry × strike) surface.
description:
Each option's vega is summed into its (expiry, strike) bucket. Total vega is
conserved — the surface sum equals the input vega sum.

name: volatility_surface_implied_vol
summary: Back out the implied-volatility surface from market option prices.
description:
For each quoted option the Black-Scholes equation is inverted for implied
volatility by bisection. Round-tripping (pricing at the recovered IV)
reproduces the input price.

name: volga_vega_convexity
summary: Volga (vomma) — convexity of value in volatility (∂²V/∂σ² = ∂vega/∂σ).
description:
``Volga = vega · d1 · d2 / σ``. Identical for calls and puts. Positive volga
means the position is long volatility-of-volatility.

name: advanced_measurement_approach_ama
summary: Advanced Measurement Approach (AMA) capital charge — retired under Basel III/IV.
description:
Superseded by the Standardised Measurement Approach for Basel III/IV
regulatory capital (see ``basel_standardised_measurement_sma``); retained
here for economic-capital, internal scenario analysis, and jurisdictions
still on earlier timelines only.

The AMA permits the LDA internal model. Under Basel II §669(b), if a bank can
demonstrate that expected loss (EL) is already captured in its provisioning /
pricing, capital may be set to unexpected loss only (OpVaR − EL); otherwise
capital equals the full OpVaR.

name: audit_finding_risk_scorer
summary: Score an outstanding audit finding by severity, likelihood and ageing.
description:
Base score is severity × likelihood on the 5×5 scale; overdue remediation
escalates the score (each 30-day block adds an uplift), capped at 25.

name: basel_standardised_measurement_sma
summary: Basel III Standardised Measurement Approach (SMA) capital.
description:
SMA capital = BIC × ILM, where the Business Indicator Component (BIC) is a
piecewise-linear function of the Business Indicator (12%/15%/18% marginal
coefficients across the three buckets) and the Internal Loss Multiplier
(ILM) scales by the bank's historical loss experience:
``ILM = ln(e − 1 + (LC / BIC)^0.8)``. Bucket-1 banks may set ILM = 1.

name: business_continuity_risk_score
summary: Business-continuity risk from RTO/RPO versus tolerance and BCP maturity.
description:
Flags where the recovery time objective (RTO) exceeds the maximum tolerable
downtime (MTD) and discounts the residual risk by BCP maturity. A breach of
MTD is the dominant driver.

name: business_environment_factor_bei
summary: Business Environment Indicator (BEI) capital adjustment multiplier.
description:
Translates forward-looking business-environment factor scores (e.g. on a 1-5
scale where higher = riskier) into a capital multiplier around 1.0: scores
above the baseline increase capital, below decrease it. Part of the BEICF
overlay permitted under the AMA.

name: compound_loss_distribution
summary: Simulate the compound (aggregate) annual loss distribution.
description:
The classic frequency ⊗ severity convolution: for each simulated year draw a
Poisson(lambda) number of events, then that many lognormal(mu, sigma)
severities, and sum. Per RULE 3 all randomness is pre-drawn in pure Python;
the per-year aggregation runs in the JIT kernel.

name: conduct_risk_metric
summary: Composite conduct-risk metric from complaints and redress intensity.
description:
Combines the complaints-per-1000-customers rate and the redress-to-revenue
ratio into a normalised 0-100 conduct-risk index (higher = worse) with a RAG
band.

name: control_testing_effectiveness
summary: Control testing pass rate and effectiveness conclusion.
description:
The empirical pass rate from control testing samples; an exception rate above
a supervisory tolerance (default >5% failures) downgrades the conclusion.

name: cyber_risk_loss_estimation
summary: Estimate expected and worst-case cyber loss.
description:
Worst-case (given a breach) = ``records_exposed × cost_per_record +
business_interruption_cost``; expected loss multiplies by the annual breach
probability — a FAIR-style single-loss-expectancy estimate.

name: diversification_benefit_oprisk
summary: Diversification benefit across OpRisk cells under a single correlation.
description:
Compares the simple sum of standalone capitals (perfect-correlation, no
diversification) with the correlated aggregate
``sqrt(sum_i sum_j rho_ij K_i K_j)`` using a uniform pairwise correlation.
The benefit is the reduction from imperfect correlation.

name: escalation_threshold_calculation
summary: Determine the escalation level for a loss against tiered thresholds.
description:
Maps a loss amount to the highest governance tier whose threshold it meets or
exceeds (e.g. ``{"team": 1e3, "head": 1e4, "exco": 1e5, "board": 1e6}``).

name: external_loss_data_integration
summary: Integrate scaled external loss data with internal data.
description:
External (consortium / public) losses are scaled to the firm's size by a
``scaling_factor`` (e.g. ratio of revenues) before being pooled with internal
losses — the standard approach for enriching a sparse internal tail.

name: frequency_distribution_fitting
summary: Fit a Poisson frequency distribution to annual loss-event counts.
description:
The Poisson MLE for lambda is the sample mean of annual counts. Also reports
the variance-to-mean ratio (dispersion) — a value far above 1 signals
over-dispersion and a possible negative-binomial alternative.

name: insurance_offset_calculation
summary: Insurance mitigation offset for an operational loss.
description:
Recoverable amount = ``min(max(gross_loss − deductible, 0), policy_limit)``
reduced by a supervisory haircut (Basel caps total insurance recognition at
20% of capital and applies haircuts for residual term and payment
uncertainty; the cap is applied by the caller).

name: internal_control_factor_icf
summary: Internal Control Factor (ICF) capital adjustment multiplier.
description:
Stronger internal controls (higher average effectiveness in [0, 1]) reduce
